target.title: fix(ssh-tunnel): handle spawn error to prevent unhandled rejection crash
target.body:
## Summary

Add a child-process `error` listener in `startSshPortForward` so missing `/usr/bin/ssh` (ENOENT) rejects the tunnel Promise instead of emitting an unhandled error that crashes the process.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: `spawn("/usr/bin/ssh", ...)` emits async `error` event. Without a listener, Node.js throws an unhandled `error` event and crashes the process. The existing `child.once("exit", ...)` never fires on spawn failure, so the `Promise.race` hangs until timeout.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, OpenClaw main

**Exact steps run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The new test "rejects with the spawn error when ssh binary is missing" constructs a mock child that emits `error` via `queueMicrotask`, matching real asynchronous spawn behavior, and verifies the tunnel start Promise rejects with "ENOENT".

**Before-fix evidence**: `child.once("exit", ...)` was the only listener. A spawn ENOENT would emit `error` asynchronously, the `exit` listener would never fire, and the unhandled `error` event would crash the process.

**Observed result after fix**: `child.once("error", reject)` forwards spawn failures into the Promise rejection path. The `Promise.race` rejects with the ENOENT error instead of hanging.

**What was not tested**: Live system without `/usr/bin/ssh` (not possible in CI). The test verifies the exact Node.js spawn error contract.

## Risk

Low. One-line addition in an existing Promise constructor. Does not change the happy path.
